newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's ATX index powered higher by OMV gains.
newsitem.headline: Austria's ATX index powered higher by OMV gains.

text.p: Austrian shares shook off a weakish start to end with solid gains on Monday thanks to spirited demand for market heavyweight OMV, the oil and energy group.

Opinions are divided on the short-term direction of the market, with some saying the ATX index's next target is 1,330 points, while others feel a consolidation around today's closing level is more likely.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips ended 20.33 points, or 1.59 percent, higher at 1,300.35 after earlier slipping to as low as 1,274.59.
Traders said a buoyant dollar and firm international leads helped encourage buying.
"We're now going to pause for breath and then set off again," said one trader, who sees the ATX testing 1,330 points this week.
But another trader voiced concern over the uncertainty surrounding France and its Euro agenda as well as the gold row in Germany and its ramifications.
"The ATX is open in both directions," the trader said, forecasting a trading range of between 1,260 and 1,320 points.
Gainers outpaced decliners, with 16 ATX shares higher and five lower.
The day's best performing ATX stock was OMV, up 4.61 percent or 70 schillings at 1,589 on a short squeeze after a huge buy order unleashed a barrage of catch-up buying from market makers.
The leading decliner was Creditanstalt ordinaries, down 2.82 percent or 20 schillings at 688.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index advanced 1.15 percent to 477.36 points.
The June ATX future added on 25.3 points to 1,301.3 on turnover of 24,535 contracts.
